precepts.text: Thou shalt carry much seed into the field and gather but little in, for the locust shall consume it, which is exactly what Joel just read.
precepts.point: This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
“That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten”. This is the plague coming on the crops through the locusts and cankerworms, and it is a curse: “Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field, and shalt gather but little in; for the locust shall consume it.” That is exactly what Joel just read.

This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

precepts.text: Thou shalt plant vineyards and dress them but neither drink of the wine nor gather the grapes, for the worms shall eat them.
precepts.point: This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
The curse keeps going, the way Joel's plague does: “Thou shalt plant vineyards, and dress them, but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes; for the worms shall eat them.” What the locust left the cankerworm eats, and what the cankerworm left the caterpiller eats, right down to the vineyards.

This fell on Israel going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards to plant and dress. You do not usually hear these curses brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

precepts.text: Set up the standard toward Zion, for the Most High will bring evil and a great destruction from the north.
precepts.point: A nation has come up upon his land, strong and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and the cheek teeth of a great lion. This is how we know the time period; if you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why: “For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number”. Jeremiah shows where it came from: “Set up the standard toward Zion: retire, stay not: for I will bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.” The Most High himself brings the evil and the great destruction from the north. The nation that came up upon the land is the one he brings out of the north, and that is how we know the time period.

precepts.text: The lion is come up from his thicket and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way to make the land desolate; this is not Christ but a nation that is not us coming to lay Israel's cities waste.
precepts.point: A nation has come up upon his land, strong and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and the cheek teeth of a great lion. This is how we know the time period; if you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
Joel's nation has “the teeth of a lion” and “the cheek teeth of a great lion.” Jeremiah names the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

This is not Christ. It is a nation that is not us, coming to lay Israel's cities waste without an inhabitant. If you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon, and that is how we know the time period.

precepts.text: The Most High brings Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north; Babylon is called the destroyer of the Gentiles because the Most High used them as a sword against Tyrus and the other heathen nations, not just against Israel.
precepts.point: A nation has come up upon his land, strong and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and the cheek teeth of a great lion. This is how we know the time period; if you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will bring upon Tyrus Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north, with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, and companies, and much people.” The lion from the north is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, and the Most High is the one who brings him.

Babylon is called the destroyer of the Gentiles because the Most High used them as a sword against Tyrus and the other heathen nations, not just against Israel. That is the nation strong and without number that came up upon the land, the lion of Daniel, Babylon.

points: The word of the Lord came to Joel the son of Pethuel. Because this opening does not name a king, the scholars had issues determining the time period, but precept upon precept shows us when it was.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The Most High tells the old men and all the inhabitants of the land to hear this and to ask whether the like has been in their days or the days of their fathers.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: Tell your children of it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation. What is about to come on the crops is to be handed down from generation to generation.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: That which the palmerworm left the locust ate, and that which the locust left the cankerworm ate, and that which the cankerworm left the caterpillar ate. This is the plague coming on the crops through the locusts and cankerworms.

This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: Awake ye drunkards and weep, and howl all ye drinkers of wine, because the new wine is cut off from your mouth. The new wine is cut off because the palmerworms and cankerworms ate up the vineyards where the grapes for the wine were grown, exactly as Deuteronomy 28:39 said.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: A nation has come up upon his land, strong and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and the cheek teeth of a great lion. This is how we know the time period; if you are familiar with the book of Daniel, the nation represented as the lion is Babylon.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The enemy laid the vine waste and barked the fig tree, making it clean bare. The land mourns because the corn is wasted, the new wine is dried up, and the oil languishes.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The meat offering and the drink offering are cut off from the house of the Lord, and the priests, the Lord's ministers, mourn.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The husbandmen and vinedressers are ashamed because the harvest of the field is perished; the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, the palm, and the apple tree are all withered, and joy is withered away from the sons of men.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The Most High calls the priests to gird themselves and lament, to sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants into the house of the Lord, and cry unto him.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The day of the Lord is at hand and shall come as a destruction from the Almighty; the meat is cut off, the seed is rotten, the barns are broken down, and the beasts and cattle groan because they have no pasture.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

points: The prophet cries unto the Lord because the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness and the rivers of waters are dried up.
